_meta.purpose: Every external reference this project relies on, with what it was used to establish and how it was checked. site/sources.html renders this file; verify_site.py audits it. A row with verified=false must not be used to support a published number.
_meta.policy: Official = kalshi.com, docs.kalshi.com, demo.kalshi.co or a source Kalshi itself names in a settlement field. Anything else is third-party and is only ever recorded as context, never as verification.
_meta.network_note: Every docs.kalshi.com and demo-API read listed here was retrieved through the agent's fetch path. Direct shell egress to kalshi.co failed in this sandbox (see FLAG-12), which is why raw responses are archived under data/ instead of being re-fetchable by clicking a link on the deployed site.

items.establishes: Demo REST base https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 (alt https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2); production external-api.kalshi.com (alt api.elections.kalshi.com); demo WS wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2.
Demo account has mock funds; keys are not shared between demo and production; demo prices and behaviour may not reflect real markets; the endpoints table this project's host list was copied from.

Signature string = timestamp + METHOD + path-including-/trade-api/v2 (query excluded); RSA-PSS SHA-256 with salt length equal to digest length, or Ed25519 over the raw message; base64; headers KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY / -TIMESTAMP / -SIGNATURE.
API key usage and the fact that a key is created in the account's own environment; keys can be scoped, including read::portfolio_balance.
A key is registered by uploading your own RSA or Ed25519 public key in PEM; verification is RSA-PSS-SHA256 or Ed25519 accordingly.

Every WS connection requires the signed handshake (message timestamp + GET + /trade-api/ws/v2); public vs private channel lists; error 9 when a market-data-only key subscribes to a private channel; server pings after 10 s idle; subscribe frame shape.

Token bucket, default 10 tokens/request, separate Read and Write budgets, 3-second burst window at Basic/Advanced, 429 body {"error":{"code":"too_many_requests"}} with no Retry-After, per-shard write buckets, X-RateLimit-* headers.
Cursor-based pagination convention used by /markets and /markets/trades.
Exchange indexes and that a market lives on exactly one shard, which is why cancels need market_ticker routing.
Shape of the status response, including trading_active and per-index status.
Official statement that there is a short delay before exchange events are reflected in API endpoints, and the recommendation to combine writes with WS data.
Scheduled maintenance and pause states a market can be in; relevant to a dashboard that claims liveness.

Per-subaccount balances are readable in one call and return only existing subaccount/exchange-index pairs, including zero balances — which is why the single /portfolio/balance breakdown is sufficient here and what a change to subaccounts would cost.

groups.title: Market data endpoints the dashboard is built on

items.establishes: The complete official category/tag taxonomy. Read live: 17 real categories + Test, harrison-test and a null entry; no Culture; no retail-gasoline category.
category/tags filters are exact and case-sensitive; include_volume adds volume_fp; there is no limit or cursor; volume_fp is contracts; fee_type values include quadratic and the maker-fee variants.

limit 1-1000 default 100; min_ts/max_ts are integer seconds (milliseconds are a 400); an unknown ticker returns 200 with an empty list; block trades are included and marked is_block_trade; taker_side is deprecated in favour of taker_outcome_side/taker_book_side; both parties trade at one price.

status filter vocabulary (unopened|open|closed|settled), one status at a time, timestamp filters mutually exclusive with some status filters, the response is cached briefly, and the market object fields the tables display.
Single-market read, including result / settlement_ts / settlement_value_dollars and the note that the response is cached for a short time.
limit ≤ 200; status enum; tickers/series_ticker/with_nested_markets; min_close_ts and min_updated_ts are seconds; multivariate events excluded; collateral_return_type values MECNET|DIRECNET.

orderbook_fp returns yes_dollars and no_dollars as [price_dollars, count_fp] pairs, ascending, best last, bids only; a YES bid at X is an ask at 1-X; depth=N; empty book and unknown ticker are both 200-with-empty; it is a point-in-time snapshot.
The endpoint's own statement that no asks are returned, which is the justification for printing an implied ask rather than a data field.

period_interval accepts only 1, 60 or 1440 minutes; start_ts/end_ts in seconds; ≤5,000 periods per response; fields are end_period_ts, volume_fp, open_interest_fp and OHLC dollar strings; pre-cutoff history lives under /historical.
Event-level aggregated candles exist — the reason the unused-endpoint list is honest rather than a gap.
Event-keyed live data exists for crypto price charts and commodity price timeseries — the closest official 'underlying price' feed, and the candidate answer to the gas-price instrument question.
Prices and quantities are fixed-point decimal strings; count 0-2 dp in requests, price 2-4 dp, responses up to 6 dp.
What falls out of the live data set over time and where it goes (/historical/*), which bounds how far the resolution ledger can be back-filled.
A batch order-book endpoint exists, which is how a multi-market ladder should be built once the dashboard shows more than one book.
Batch candle retrieval for multiple markets in one request.
GET /events excludes multivariate events and this is the documented endpoint that returns them, which is the whole basis for the Q-07 exclusion decision.
An official way to enumerate the filters available per sport, which is the correct way to confirm the golf selector rather than guessing tags.

V2 request shape; BookSide quotes the YES leg only (bid = buy YES, ask = sell YES = buy NO at 1−price); FixedPointCount minimum 0.01; valid prices constrained by the market's price-level structure; self_trade_prevention_type ∈ {taker_at_cross, maker}; remaining_count is the final state for IOC; average_fill_price/average_fee_paid only when fill_count > 0; default write cost 10 tokens; legacy /portfolio/orders writes are 410 Gone.
Cancel returns {order_id, client_order_id, reduced_by}; auto-routing needs market_ticker with exchange_index omitted or -1; cancelling against the wrong shard is an error.
Amend sets the updated total/max-fillable count (filled + desired resting); an amend that changes nothing is a 400.
Exactly one of reduce_by or reduce_to.
How direction is expressed on Order, Fill and Trade via outcome_side and book_side, and how to migrate off the legacy action/side fields.

Fill field list (fill_id, exchange_index, trade_id, order_id, ticker, market_ticker, outcome_side, book_side, count_fp, yes_price_dollars, no_price_dollars, is_taker, fee_cost, created_time, subaccount_number, ts); a bid ≡ yes; buy-YES and sell-NO both report outcome_side yes; deprecated fields stay until at least 2026-05-14; pre-cutoff fills only via /historical/fills.

balance is integer cents, balance_dollars is a string, portfolio_value has no documented dollars sibling, balance_breakdown covers every exchange index across subaccounts including zeros, scope read::portfolio_balance, one-second budget at Basic/Advanced, and the instruction to react to fills instead of polling.
Positions returned include closed markets awaiting settlement, which may still hold non-zero quantity and cost basis — check the market's own status for trading state.
Winner is paid notional_value_dollars per contract on net positions; settlement fee is 0 for a simple yes/no binary; payouts are rounded to cents.
Creation → open → close → settlement transitions the tracker polls on, including can_close_early.
How fees and balances are rounded — the reason this project never reconstructs a fee from a multiplier.
Settlement records exist in the live data set only; archived ones move to /historical/positions.
The authoritative per-endpoint token cost table for anything non-default.
An account's tier and token-bucket budgets are readable, so a polling interval can be sized rather than guessed.
The end-to-end order flow this project mirrors: find markets, place an order, check status, cancel. Also the reference for the create→read→cancel sequence the paper engine reproduces.
Queue position is contracts-to-be-matched before a partial or full fill, by price-time priority — the reason a resting maker order's wait is knowable and could be shown in the UI.
Order reads are restricted by status (resting|canceled|executed) and canceled/executed orders before the cutoff move to /historical/orders, while resting orders always remain readable.
Order reads update asynchronously after a write, so a just-created order can briefly 404 — the documented reason to trust the write response over a follow-up read.

A batch create endpoint exists, its maximum size scales with the tier's write budget, and the batch is NOT atomic (a 201 can contain per-order failures) — the documented reason this project keeps single-order writes so a partial reject cannot be misread as success.
